evidence: The structural core exists and works: src/Forge.App/MauiProgram.cs:20-110 boots DevExpress in the correct order behind a themed shell; src/Forge.App/Hosting/AppShell.xaml:27-38 renders five tab destinations; src/Forge.App/Features/FeatureRegistration.cs:47-74 composes 22 self-registering feature modules; src/Forge.Core/Abstractions/INavigationService.cs is a MAUI-free navigation abstraction with 46 route constants in src/Forge.App/Navigation/ForgeRoutes.cs. F01.01 and F01.02 are largely delivered.
gaps: F01.03 is almost entirely absent: there is no src/Forge.Infrastructure/Diagnostics directory, no file log sink, no rotation, no redaction policy, no global exception handler, no recovery screen and no OnSleep/OnResume state persistence. Grep for 'GlobalExceptionHandler|UnhandledException|UnobservedTaskException|RecoveryPage|FileLoggerProvider|ForgeLogEvents' over src/ returns zero matches. The epic outcome sentence 'logs structurally ... survives suspend and resume with state intact, and fails gracefully with a recoverable error surface rather than a crash' is unmet on all three counts.

evidence: Forge.slnx declares four src projects and three test projects; src/Directory.Build.targets:14-34 implements the compiler-enforced architecture guard (FORGE001/FORGE002) and tests/Forge.Core.Tests/Architecture/DependencyRuleTests.cs:33-51 backs it at the assembly level. Directory.Packages.props is the only version source - no PackageReference in src/ or tests/ carries an inline Version attribute. src/Forge.App/MauiProgram.cs:35-70 sets ThemeManager before CreateBuilder and chains all six DevExpress registrations after UseMauiApp. src/Forge.App/Features/FeatureRegistration.cs is the single delimited registration list.
gaps: The Forge.Health project required by S01.01.01 does not exist; health code lives in src/Forge.App/Services/Health instead. No Forge.App test project exists, so no ViewModel or shell behaviour is covered by any test.

evidence: Forge.slnx lists src/Forge.App, src/Forge.Core, src/Forge.Domain, src/Forge.Infrastructure and tests/Forge.Core.Tests, tests/Forge.Domain.Tests, tests/Forge.Infrastructure.Tests. src/Forge.App/Forge.App.csproj:20-21 sets TargetFrameworks to net10.0-android plus net10.0-ios (the latter conditioned off on Linux with an in-file explanation about NETSDK1178); no Windows or Mac Catalyst TFM appears anywhere. Lines 42-43 set SupportedOSPlatformVersion 26.0 for Android and 15.0 for iOS, meeting the minimum-SDK requirement. src/Directory.Build.targets:27-33 raises MSBuild errors FORGE001 (forbidden Microsoft.Maui*/DevExpress* PackageReference) and FORGE002 (inverted ProjectReference) for Forge.Domain and Forge.Core, satisfying AC2. A repository-wide scan of src/*/*.csproj and tests/*/*.csproj found no PackageReference with an inline Version attribute, so all versions resolve from Directory.Packages.props.
gaps: REQ1 unmet: there is no Forge.Health project under src/ and no Forge.Health.Tests under tests/. Health code sits in src/Forge.App/Services/Health and src/Forge.Core/Abstractions/Health, so the layer the requirement names as a separate assembly was never created. Also, there is no Forge.App test project, so 'matching unit test projects' holds for three of the four assemblies that do exist. AC1 ('zero warnings') and AC2/AC3 as build outcomes were not executed - this is a read-only verification and a full multi-TFM build was out of scope; note that Directory.Build.props only sets TreatWarningsAsErrors when ContinuousIntegrationBuild is true, so a local zero-warning build is not enforced. AC3's literal wording ('exactly net10.0-android and net10.0-ios') is satisfied on Windows and macOS but not on Linux, where the conditional drops iOS.

evidence: src/Forge.App/MauiProgram.cs:35-36 assigns ThemeManager.UseAndroidSystemColor = false and ThemeManager.Theme = new Theme(Color.FromArgb(ForgeBrand.SeedHex)) as the first non-instrumentation statements in CreateMauiApp, before MauiApp.CreateBuilder() on line 40, exactly as the requirement demands. Lines 50-70 chain .UseMauiApp(...) followed by .UseDevExpress(useLocalization: false), .UseDevExpressControls(), .UseDevExpressCollectionView(), .UseDevExpressEditors(), .UseDevExpressCharts() and .UseDevExpressGauges() - all six required suites, all after UseMauiApp, in a single chained expression so analyzer DXM001 sees the syntactic relationship it checks (the in-file comment on lines 44-49 records why the chain must not be split). src/Forge.App/Branding/ForgeBrand.cs supplies the seed colour, and src/Forge.App/Hosting/AppShell.xaml:20-24 consumes the derived palette through dx:ThemeColor roles rather than hex literals.

The convention is real and universally applied: src/Forge.App/Features/FeatureRegistration.cs:47-74 calls 22 Add<Name>Feature extension methods in one alphabetical block, and MauiProgram.cs:95-97 reduces the shared surface to three lines (AddForgeInfrastructure, AddForgeShell, AddForgeFeatures). Each feature owns its registration file - e.g. src/Forge.App/Features/Onboarding/OnboardingFeatureRegistration.cs:24-63 registers its pages and view models transient (lines 28-31), its stores singleton (line 32), and registers its own routes (lines 59-60). src/Forge.App/Composition/InfrastructureRegistration.cs:46-50 registers ForgeDbContext transient with a documented rationale, and lines 57-61 register IDataSessionFactory singleton, satisfying the DbContext-lifetime requirement.
gaps: AC1's 'the only conflicting line is within the delimited registration block' is undermined by a live counter-example: AppShell is bound twice - src/Forge.App/MauiProgram.cs:124 (services.AddSingleton<AppShell>()) and src/Forge.App/Features/Onboarding/OnboardingFeatureRegistration.cs:34-57 (a factory that attaches FirstRunGate to shell.Loaded). Because AddForgeFeatures runs after AddForgeShell, the Onboarding binding silently wins. This is the same failure shape as the IDataErasureService double-binding: correctness depends on registration order rather than being stated, and a second feature registering AppShell would silently displace first-run routing with no build or test failure. AC2 ('all dependencies resolve without a runtime resolution exception') cannot be grounded by reading - it needs a container validation pass or a device launch, and there is no Forge.App test project that would catch it.

evidence: src/Forge.App/Hosting/AppShell.xaml:27-38 declares a five-destination TabBar; src/Forge.Core/Abstractions/INavigationService.cs declares GoToAsync/GoBackAsync/ShowModalAsync with no MAUI types; src/Forge.App/Navigation/ForgeRoutes.cs holds 46 route constants and 21 feature registration files call Routing.RegisterRoute against them, so call sites use constants rather than magic strings.
gaps: The feature outcome promises 'correct hardware back behaviour on Android' for modal flows. ShowModalAsync is dead code (no caller in src/) and its //route implementation cannot work for a globally registered route; nothing intercepts hardware back; nothing restores scroll position. Tabs carry no icons, so tab selection is conveyed by colour alone.

evidence: src/Forge.App/Hosting/AppShell.xaml:27-38 declares exactly the five required destinations - Today, Train, Nutrition, Progress, Profile - each with a Route matching a ForgeRoutes constant and a ContentTemplate pointing at a real page type. Lines 20-24 style the tab bar from DevExpress semantic roles (SurfaceContainer, Primary, OnSurfaceVariant), so light/dark follows the theme rather than hex literals. src/Forge.App/Hosting/AppShell.xaml.cs:7-11 sets BindingContext from the injected AppShellViewModel.
gaps: REQ1 unmet as written: navigation uses MAUI Shell's TabBar, not dx:TabView. The XAML comment on lines 14-18 argues Shell owns routing and back stack while TabView is a content control - a defensible call - but docs/architecture/overview.md:79 still states 'Primary navigation | dx:TabView', so the codebase contradicts its own architecture document and no ADR records the change. REQ2/AC1 unmet: no ShellContent carries an Icon, so tab selection is signalled by colour alone (TabBarTitleColor vs TabBarUnselectedColor). That fails WCAG 1.4.1 and directly contradicts AC1's 'conveyed by both an icon change and a colour change'. REQ3/AC2 unmet: nothing persists or restores the selected tab. AppShellViewModel.SelectedTabIndex (src/Forge.App/Hosting/AppShellViewModel.cs:17-18) is declared and documented as 'Persisted on suspend' but is never read or written anywhere in src/, and AppShell.xaml binds nothing to it - it is write-only-never-even-written state. App.xaml.cs has no OnSleep or OnResume override. A process kill always returns the user to Today. AC3 (screen-reader announcement) is only partly grounded: no SemanticProperties are set on any ShellContent, so announcements depend entirely on the platform reading Title; selected-state announcement is not asserted anywhere. AC4 (gesture-navigation safe area) cannot be judged by reading and needs a device.

evidence: src/Forge.Core/Abstractions/INavigationService.cs:11-31 declares the interface in Forge.Core with exactly GoToAsync, GoBackAsync and ShowModalAsync, taking object? for the parameter so no dictionary appears at the call site. tests/Forge.Core.Tests/Architecture/DependencyRuleTests.cs:54-68 asserts no framework namespace leaks into any INavigationService signature, which grounds the substitutability requirement. src/Forge.App/Navigation/ForgeRoutes.cs declares all 46 destinations as constants and every Routing.RegisterRoute call across 21 feature registration files uses those constants. src/Forge.App/Navigation/ShellNavigationService.cs:36-54 marshals the typed parameter into Shell's dictionary under a single private key and throws a descriptive InvalidOperationException when Shell.Current is null.
gaps: AC1 unmet in practice: no ViewModel test with a substituted INavigationService exists anywhere - there is no Forge.App test project, and grep for INavigationService across tests/ matches only DependencyRuleTests. The abstraction is testable; nothing tests through it. AC2 unmet: ShellNavigationService performs no route validation at all - it forwards straight to Shell.GoToAsync, so the exception a caller sees is whatever MAUI raises, not a Forge exception that names the offending route, and no test pins the message. AC3 unmet and structurally broken: ShowModalAsync (line 26-27) prefixes the route with '//', which in MAUI Shell means an absolute route that resets the navigation stack to a Shell item - but every non-tab destination in Forge is a global route registered with Routing.RegisterRoute, and MAUI refuses an absolute navigation whose only page is a global route. Worse, ShowModalAsync has no caller anywhere in src/ (grep finds only the interface declaration and the implementation); pages that need modal presentation instead set Shell.TabBarIsVisible="False" on themselves - e.g. src/Forge.App/Features/Workout/ActiveWorkoutPage.xaml:10 - and are reached with ordinary GoToAsync. Nothing intercepts the Android hardware back button and nothing preserves the underlying tab's scroll position.

evidence: Grep over src/ for 'GlobalExceptionHandler|UnhandledException|UnobservedTaskException|RecoveryPage|FileLoggerProvider|ForgeLogEvents' returns zero matches. src/Forge.Infrastructure has no Diagnostics directory (its only folders are Backup, Content, Media and Persistence). The only logging configuration in the app is src/Forge.App/MauiProgram.cs:101-103, a DEBUG-only builder.Logging.AddDebug(). The only failure surface is src/Forge.App/App.xaml.cs:57-62, which writes a startup fault to Debug.WriteLine and its own comment defers the user-facing surface to 'the recovery surface (E01/F01.03)' - which does not exist.
gaps: None of the three stories in this feature is delivered. There is no file log sink, no rotation, no redaction rule, no exception boundary, no recovery screen, no diagnostic-sharing consent flow and no suspend/resume state snapshot. The feature outcome - 'a crash-free-feeling app where unexpected failures produce a recoverable screen and a local diagnostic record the user can choose to share' - has no implementation behind it.

evidence: The implementation notes point at src/Forge.Infrastructure/Diagnostics/FileLoggerProvider.cs and ForgeLogEvents.cs. Neither file exists; src/Forge.Infrastructure contains only Backup/, Content/, Media/ and Persistence/. Grep over src/ for ILoggerProvider or AddLogging returns no provider registration of any kind. The complete logging configuration is src/Forge.App/MauiProgram.cs:101-103: '#if DEBUG builder.Logging.AddDebug(); #endif'. Structured source-generated logging is used correctly where it is used - src/Forge.App/Composition/ForgeStartup.cs:177-187 declares four [LoggerMessage] events - but in a Release build those events go nowhere because no provider is registered.
gaps: Every requirement is unmet. No file sink writes to the app cache directory (REQ1). No rotation at 5 MB and no three-file retention exists anywhere (REQ2, AC2). No redaction rule or policy prevents bodyweight, heart rate, food names or free-text notes from being logged - there is no allow-list, no scrubber and no test asserting their absence (REQ3, AC1). Release builds have no sink at all, so REQ5's 'Debug builds additionally log to the platform debug console' is inverted: Debug is the only build that logs. AC3 (no frame exceeding 16.6 ms attributable to logging) cannot be judged by reading and would need on-device frame timing; it is moot while no sink exists.

evidence: The implementation notes point at src/Forge.App/Diagnostics/GlobalExceptionHandler.cs and src/Forge.App/Features/Diagnostics/RecoveryPage.xaml. Neither file nor either directory exists - src/Forge.App has no Diagnostics folder and Features/ has no Diagnostics subfolder. Grep over src/ for UnhandledException, UnobservedTaskException, AppDomain.CurrentDomain or TaskScheduler returns no handler registration. ForgeRoutes.cs declares no recovery route, so there is nothing to navigate to. The closest thing to a failure surface is src/Forge.App/App.xaml.cs:53-63, which swallows a startup failure into System.Diagnostics.Debug.WriteLine and explicitly defers user presentation to this story.
gaps: All five requirements are unmet. Nothing captures UI-thread unhandled exceptions or unobserved task exceptions, so an unhandled exception terminates the process (AC1 unmet). There is no recovery screen and therefore no Continue, Restart or Share diagnostics affordance (AC2, AC3 unmet). There is no diagnostic payload, no preview-before-share confirmation and no transmission path - the last of which means REQ5 ('no automatic transmission') is trivially true but for the wrong reason. Note the interaction with the workout flush requirement: src/Forge.App/Features/Workout/WorkoutPersistenceService.cs does commit sets to the database as they are logged, so in-progress work would survive a crash, but that is incidental to this story rather than the flush-on-boundary it specifies.

evidence: The in-progress-workout half of this story is genuinely delivered, though by a different mechanism than specified: src/Forge.App/Features/Workout/WorkoutPersistenceService.cs:166-260 writes ActiveWorkoutState and each logged set to the encrypted database as they happen, and lines 146-163 reload the state on next launch, classifying it with Forge.Domain.Workout.WorkoutRecoveryPolicy.Classify. src/Forge.Domain/Workout/WorkoutRecoveryPolicy.cs:8 sets DefaultStaleAfter = TimeSpan.FromHours(12), matching the story's 12-hour rule, and src/Forge.App/Features/Workout/ActiveWorkoutPageViewModel.cs:792-798 surfaces Resume and Stale outcomes to the user. So AC1 - three logged sets present after a process kill - is satisfied by continuous write-through rather than by an OnSleep snapshot.
gaps: The navigation half is entirely missing. src/Forge.App/App.xaml.cs overrides only CreateWindow and OnStart - there is no OnSleep or OnResume override anywhere in src/, so nothing persists on suspend as REQ1 requires. The named artefact src/Forge.App/Shell/AppStateSnapshot.cs does not exist. Selected tab and active route are never captured: AppShellViewModel.SelectedTabIndex (src/Forge.App/Hosting/AppShellViewModel.cs:17-18) is declared with the comment 'Persisted on suspend' and is neither read nor written by any other file, and AppShell.xaml binds nothing to it. AC2 is only accidentally satisfied - the app always opens on Today because no tab is ever restored, not because stale state is discarded; and the 13-hour workout case shows a 'finish it now or discard it' prompt rather than being discarded silently. Separately, src/Forge.App/Features/Workout/ActiveWorkoutDraftStore.cs implements a Preferences-backed draft store and is registered at WorkoutFeatureRegistration.cs:30, but no type injects IActiveWorkoutDraftStore - it is registered dead code, and it applies no staleness rule of its own. AC3 (restoration adding no more than 100 ms to cold start) cannot be judged by reading, and is moot while restoration does not exist.

evidence: The encrypted storage core is real and well built. src/Forge.Infrastructure/Persistence/ForgeDbContext.cs discovers mappings from IEntityTypeConfiguration and applies a central soft-delete filter (lines 49-66); Directory.Packages.props pins Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Sqlite.Core plus SQLitePCLRaw.bundle_e_sqlcipher 2.1.11 with a comment recording the plaintext-shipping incident; tests/Forge.Infrastructure.Tests/Persistence/DatabaseEncryptionTests.cs proves encryption by inspecting bytes on disk rather than trusting the library. 47 HasIndex declarations across 11 configuration files cover the hot query shapes. src/Forge.Core/Abstractions/Data/ holds a clean, EF-free repository and session abstraction that 13 app services use.
gaps: Three whole areas are missing or inert. (1) F04.05 - corruption detection and recovery - has no scheduled integrity cadence, no safety-copy service and no operation journal; grep for 'quick_check|OperationJournal|SafetyCopy|abnormal' over src/ returns one hit, the startup integrity_check. (2) Scale is not addressed anywhere: no 50,000-set or 100,000-food fixture exists in tests/, no QueryPlanTests.cs exists, and IRepository<T> exposes no query surface at all - ListAsync materialises the entire table, so the food catalogue is loaded in full on every keystroke. (3) The epic's own performance premise is contradicted by its own documentation: docs/security/database-encryption.md:37-41 records 469 ms per connection open under the passphrase key form Forge uses, against S04.01.01 AC1's 50 ms budget, and Forge opens a context per operation. Also: no concurrency tokens exist on any entity, and the shipped catalogues are 60 exercises and 30 foods against backlog figures of 2,000 and 100,000.

evidence: src/Forge.Infrastructure/Persistence/ForgeDbContextFactory.cs:33-62 builds the connection string with private cache, foreign keys on and a busy timeout, and attaches SqlitePragmaConnectionInterceptor, which issues PRAGMA key, foreign_keys, busy_timeout and journal_mode=WAL on every open (SqlitePragmaConnectionInterceptor.cs:37-51). src/Forge.Infrastructure/Persistence/SecureStorageDatabaseKeyProvider.cs:25-28 mints a 256-bit key with RandomNumberGenerator and stores it only through ISecureStorage. src/Forge.Infrastructure/Persistence/LocalDatabaseEncryption.cs converts a legacy plaintext file via sqlcipher_export into a side file and only replaces the original on success. DatabaseEncryptionTests proves the file is genuinely encrypted.
gaps: The feature outcome says Forge 'fails safely when key material is unavailable'. It does not create an empty database, but there is no recovery surface to fail into - F01.03 was never built - so a missing key surfaces as an InvalidOperationException whose Message is interpolated into user-facing text (src/Forge.App/Features/Exercises/ExerciseDataStore.cs:161-167), which the repository's own contributor rules forbid. Performance: docs/security/database-encryption.md:37-41 measures 469 ms per connection open, ten times S04.01.01's 50 ms budget.

evidence: ForgeDbContext lives at src/Forge.Infrastructure/Persistence/ForgeDbContext.cs and uses EF Core with the SQLite provider via ForgeDbContextFactory.CreateOptions (ForgeDbContextFactory.cs:17-21), satisfying REQ1. REQ2 is enforced twice over: src/Directory.Build.targets:27-33 fails the build on a forbidden package reference in Forge.Domain/Forge.Core, and tests/Forge.Core.Tests/Architecture/DependencyRuleTests.cs:33-51 asserts the compiled assemblies reference no Microsoft.Maui, DevExpress, Microsoft.UI or Xamarin assembly - which also grounds AC2. REQ3 holds: src/Forge.App/Composition/ForgeStartup.cs:25 sets DatabasePath to Path.Combine(FileSystem.AppDataDirectory, "forge.db"), never the cache directory. journal_mode=WAL plus a 5 s busy timeout (SqlitePragmaConnectionInterceptor.cs:47-49) give the crash-consistency property REQ4 asks for.
gaps: AC1 is contradicted by the project's own measurement: docs/security/database-encryption.md:37-41 and the interceptor's own remarks (SqlitePragmaConnectionInterceptor.cs:56-77) record 469 ms per connection open under the passphrase key form that is in use, versus a 5 ms unkeyed baseline - roughly ten times AC1's 50 ms budget for a SELECT 1 through ForgeDbContext. The comment states the real fix is to stop opening a connection per operation, and that has not been done: EfDataSessionFactory.Create() opens a fresh context, and callers create a session per operation. REQ5/AC4 unmet: no 50,000-set or 100,000-food fixture exists anywhere under tests/, and no query-plan assertion exists. The named file src/Forge.Infrastructure/Persistence/PersistenceRegistration.cs does not exist - registration happens in the app layer at src/Forge.App/Composition/InfrastructureRegistration.cs - which is a harmless divergence but means the backlog's path hint is wrong. AC3 (process kill at the riskiest write point) cannot be settled by reading; it would need a fault-injection run.

evidence: src/Forge.Infrastructure/Persistence/SecureStorageDatabaseKeyProvider.cs:25-28 generates exactly 32 bytes (256 bits) from System.Security.Cryptography.RandomNumberGenerator on first run and persists the base64 form through ISecureStorage under a versioned key name, satisfying REQ1 and AC1. REQ2 holds by construction: Forge.Infrastructure cannot reference MAUI, so the only writer is the ISecureStorage adapter src/Forge.App/Services/Storage/MauiSecureStorage.cs, and the key never touches Preferences, a file or source. There is no log statement anywhere that emits the key. src/Forge.App/Composition/ForgeStartup.cs:108-111 resolves the key once at startup and caches it in ForgeDatabaseOptions, which throws a descriptive InvalidOperationException rather than silently opening a second differently-keyed database (ForgeStartup.cs:32-35). REQ3's negative half is met: LocalDatabaseEncryption.EnsureEncryptedAsync returns NotNeeded when neither key form opens the file (LocalDatabaseEncryption.cs:87-92) and DatabaseInitializer returns a MigrationFailed result rather than creating an empty database.
gaps: REQ3's positive half and AC2 are unmet: 'Forge opens recovery' has nowhere to go. GetOrCreateKeyAsync mints a brand-new key whenever secure storage returns nothing, with no check for an existing database file, so the 'database exists, key missing' case is not detected as such - it is discovered later as a generic migration failure. There is no recovery screen (F01.03 was never built), so the user sees whatever each feature surface improvises; in the exercise library that is src/Forge.App/Features/Exercises/ExerciseDataStore.cs:161-163, which interpolates startup.Failure.Message into on-screen text, exactly the practice the contributor rules prohibit. AC2's '1 second' bound and the 'database timestamp unchanged' assertion are untested. REQ5/AC4: no large-scale fixture exists. AC3 (kill at the riskiest write point) is ungroundable by reading - though note LocalDatabaseEncryption.ConvertAsync:158-182 is genuinely written to be interruption-safe, writing to a .encrypting side file and only moving on success. The named file src/Forge.Core/Abstractions/Security/ISqlCipherKeyStore.cs does not exist; the equivalent is src/Forge.Core/Abstractions/Data/IDatabaseKeyProvider.cs.

evidence: tests/Forge.Infrastructure.Tests/Persistence/DatabaseEncryptionTests.cs implements all three substantive requirements and inspects the bytes on disk rather than asking the library whether it encrypted anything - the file's own remarks explain that this is precisely because PRAGMA key against stock SQLite is silently ignored. The_key_is_required_to_open_the_database_again (line 88) creates a keyed database, then opens it through ForgeDbContextFactory.CreateOptions with no key and asserts a SqliteException, satisfying REQ1 and AC1. A_keyed_database_is_not_readable_as_plain_SQLite (line 61) asserts the file does not begin with 'SQLite format 3', satisfying REQ2 and AC2, and A_keyed_database_does_not_leak_table_names_to_anyone_holding_the_file (line 74) goes further by scanning the entire file for 'CREATE TABLE' and 'UserProfile' - a strictly stronger check than the first 4 KB the requirement asks for. An_unkeyed_database_still_works (line 100) pins the unkeyed path so tooling is not broken. REQ3 is covered by CreateDatabaseAsync, which writes a UserProfile row through a keyed context and reads the schema back. Supporting coverage exists in LocalDatabaseEncryptionTests.cs and ConnectionConfigurationTests.cs.

src/Forge.Domain/Common/Entity.cs gives every entity a time-ordered GUID v7 key, CreatedUtc, ModifiedUtc and nullable DeletedUtc. ForgeDbContext.ApplySoftDeleteFilters (lines 49-66) applies the DeletedUtc IS NULL filter to every Entity subclass centrally, and StampModified (lines 90-101) maintains ModifiedUtc on every save. Three migrations exist under src/Forge.Infrastructure/Persistence/Migrations, and DatabaseInitializer.AdoptPreMigrationDatabaseAsync (lines 108-134) handles the EnsureCreated-to-Migrate transition so an existing install is not destroyed - with DatabaseSchemaParityTests asserting the equivalence that makes it safe.
gaps: No entity anywhere carries a concurrency token: grep for IsConcurrencyToken, RowVersion or IsRowVersion over src/ returns zero matches, so the typed-conflict behaviour the feature promises does not exist. Migration failure is not recorded with migration id, app version or timestamp, and there is no once-per-app-version retry guard, so a failing migration is retried on every launch. The recovery surface the feature relies on (Features/Diagnostics/DataRecoveryPage.xaml) does not exist.

evidence: The schema is real and broad. src/Forge.Infrastructure/Persistence/Configurations contains 11 configuration files covering Profile (UserProfile, BodyMetric), Training (Exercise, WorkoutSession, SetEntry), Planning (TrainingPlan, PlanDay, PlannedExercise, PlannedSet), Workout (ActiveWorkoutState), Nutrition (FoodItem, FoodLogEntry, HydrationEntry, Recipe, FoodBarcode), Recovery and Engagement (Achievement, Streak). ForgeDbContext discovers them all with ApplyConfigurationsFromAssembly (ForgeDbContext.cs:33), so REQ1 is met for nine of the ten named areas. REQ2 is met by construction: src/Forge.Domain/Common/Entity.cs:29-45 gives every entity Id (Guid.CreateVersion7), CreatedUtc, ModifiedUtc and nullable DeletedUtc, and ForgeDbContext.StampModified maintains ModifiedUtc automatically, which grounds AC2. REQ3 is met with explicit unit-carrying value types converted at the mapping boundary - src/Forge.Infrastructure/Persistence/Configurations/Training/TrainingConfigurations.cs:107-110 stores Mass as canonical kilograms with HasPrecision(10, 3) and a LoadKilograms column name, with a comment explaining that a float column could not represent a 0.25 kg micro-plate exactly.
gaps: AC1's 'all ten core aggregate areas have mapped tables' is literally false: there is no Meal entity or table. Meals are modelled as a MealSlot enum on FoodLogEntry (src/Forge.Domain/Nutrition/FoodItem.cs) and summarised in memory by NutritionPersistenceService.BuildMealSummaries. That is a defensible modelling choice, but the criterion as written is unmet and the backlog and the code should be reconciled explicitly rather than left divergent. REQ5/AC4 unmet: no 50,000-set or 100,000-food fixture exists anywhere under tests/, and no query-plan or p95 assertion exists, so the scale claim is untested. AC3 (process kill at the riskiest write point) cannot be settled by reading.

evidence: REQ1 is met: src/Forge.App/Composition/ForgeStartup.cs:128-135 runs DatabaseInitializer.InitializeAsync before anything else, and every data-backed feature awaits ForgeStartupService before querying - e.g. src/Forge.App/Features/Exercises/ExerciseDataStore.cs:152-163 - so no feature page queries ahead of migration. src/Forge.Infrastructure/Persistence/DatabaseInitializer.cs:32-41 applies migrations in order with MigrateAsync, falling back to EnsureCreatedAsync only when no migrations exist. Lines 108-134 solve the hardest real case: a database created by EnsureCreatedAsync before migrations existed has no __EFMigrationsHistory, so the baseline is recorded as already applied rather than replayed onto existing tables - the failure that would otherwise look to the user like losing all their training history. Migration failure is caught and returned as a typed DatabaseInitializationResult (lines 43-54) rather than thrown, and ForgeStartupService records it in Failure without terminating the process, which is what stops a boot loop.
gaps: REQ2 unmet: a migration failure is logged with a fixed message ('Local database migration failed; startup will enter recovery mode.') and carries no migration id, no app version and no persisted timestamp - nothing is written to the database or to a file, and in a Release build the log has no provider at all, so the record does not exist anywhere after the process ends. REQ3 unmet: there is no retry guard of any kind. InitializeAsync runs on every launch and will re-attempt the same failing migration indefinitely, once per launch, with no per-app-version marker. AC2 is unmet for a second reason: the recovery surface it names does not exist (see S01.03.02), so a relaunch after a failing migration lands on the ordinary shell with individual screens improvising an error string. The named file src/Forge.Infrastructure/Persistence/PersistenceStartupCoordinator.cs does not exist; DatabaseInitializer plus ForgeStartupService fill the role. REQ5/AC4 unmet - no scale fixture. AC3 ungroundable by reading.

evidence: REQ1 is met centrally: src/Forge.Domain/Common/Entity.cs:32 initialises CreatedUtc once via an init-only property so it cannot drift, and ForgeDbContext.StampModified (ForgeDbContext.cs:90-101) sets ModifiedUtc for every Added or Modified Entity on both SaveChanges and SaveChangesAsync. That grounds AC1 - CreatedUtc is immutable by type design and UpdatedUtc advances on each save. REQ2 is met and enforced structurally rather than per-configuration: ForgeDbContext.ApplySoftDeleteFilters (lines 49-66) walks every mapped type deriving from Entity and applies a DeletedUtc == null query filter, with a comment explaining that leaving it to each contributor would guarantee an eventual omission. Export and repair paths opt back in explicitly with IgnoreQueryFilters - src/Forge.Infrastructure/Backup/ForgeDataImporter.cs:242 and :259, and SeedContentImporter.cs:45 - which is exactly the 'included only by explicit export or repair options' the requirement asks for. EfRepository.SoftDeleteAsync (EfRepository.cs:37-47) stamps DeletedUtc rather than removing the row.
gaps: REQ3 and AC2 are entirely unmet. No entity carries a concurrency token: grep over src/ for IsConcurrencyToken, RowVersion, IsRowVersion and DbUpdateConcurrencyException finds no mapping and no handler (the single DbUpdateConcurrencyException hit, at Features/Engagement/Services/EngagementDataService.cs:155, is a comment about a missing-row update, not optimistic-concurrency handling). Entity has no version or timestamp column mapped as a token, so two contexts saving conflicting edits produce last-write-wins silently, and there is no typed conflict result anywhere in Forge.Core to return. REQ5/AC4 unmet - no 50,000-row fixture. AC3 ungroundable by reading.

evidence: Shipped content exists and imports offline: src/Forge.Infrastructure/Content/exercise-catalogue.json (60 exercises, version 2), food-catalogue.json (30 foods) and recipe-catalogue.json are embedded resources, and src/Forge.Infrastructure/Persistence/SeedContent/SeedContentImporter.cs:23-84 performs a versioned, idempotent, per-id upsert that skips user-created rows. First run therefore works with no network.
gaps: Only the exercise catalogue has a real versioned importer. Foods are seeded by an all-or-nothing helper inside a feature service (src/Forge.App/Features/Nutrition/Services/NutritionPersistenceService.cs:259-290) with no version record, no batching, no resumability and no progress status. No catalogue import records a checksum. Neither catalogue is compressed and neither ships under app raw assets as the stories specify. The 'safely apply deltas' half of the outcome holds for exercises only.

evidence: Real, careful work exists. src/Forge.Infrastructure/Persistence/SeedContent/SeedContentImporter.cs:23-84 reads a versioned catalogue, compares against a persisted SeedContentImport row and returns early when the version is unchanged (lines 30-36), then upserts each exercise by its stable catalogue GUID, explicitly skipping rows the user has marked IsUserCreated (lines 55-59). That makes the import idempotent, which grounds AC2 directly: re-running the same version changes no rows and cannot create a duplicate id. src/Forge.Infrastructure/Content/SeedCatalogue.cs:38-44 opens the embedded catalogue and ForgeStartup.cs:161-171 wires it into startup, so first run works with no network. SeedCatalogue.LoadExercises also enforces original-content provenance (lines 69-73) and fails the import rather than shipping copied third-party catalogue text. Coverage exists in SeedContentImporterTests.cs, SeedCatalogueImportTests.cs and SeedCatalogueGuidanceImportTests.cs.
gaps: REQ1 unmet in form: the catalogue is an uncompressed embedded resource in Forge.Infrastructure (Forge.Infrastructure.csproj declares Content/*.json as EmbeddedResource), not compressed JSON under src/Forge.App/Resources/Raw as the requirement and the touches path specify. REQ2 partly unmet: src/Forge.Infrastructure/Persistence/SeedContent/SeedContentImport.cs records only CatalogueName and Version - there is no checksum, so a corrupted or substituted asset at the same version is undetectable (a timestamp does come free from Entity.CreatedUtc/ModifiedUtc). AC1 fails against its stated number: the shipped catalogue contains 60 exercises, not 2,000. BACKLOG DEFECT - this is the same divergence already confirmed elsewhere in this reconciliation, where the YAML assumes a mass-imported catalogue while the product deliberately ships a small original-content set to avoid copying third-party exercise databases (SeedCatalogue.cs:9-14 states that policy). The story should not be failed for the count; it is failed for the compression/location and checksum gaps. REQ3's 3-second budget is untestable at 60 items and unmeasured. REQ5/AC4 unmet - no scale fixture. AC3 ungroundable by reading.

evidence: Neither named file exists: there is no src/Forge.Infrastructure/Catalogues directory, no FoodCatalogueImporter.cs and no IFoodCatalogueStatus.cs anywhere in the repository. What exists instead is src/Forge.App/Features/Nutrition/Services/NutritionPersistenceService.cs:259-290, a private static EnsureFoodCatalogueAsync that runs lazily on the first nutrition query: it lists every FoodItem, returns if any non-user row exists, otherwise deserialises the whole embedded food-catalogue.json in one pass (LoadSeedFoods, lines 292-308) and adds every row before a single SaveChanges. src/Forge.Infrastructure/Content/food-catalogue.json contains 30 foods.
gaps: Every requirement is unmet. REQ1: the catalogue holds 30 items, not 'at least 100,000', and the import path has no batching at all - it is one deserialise plus one SaveChanges, which would not survive a 100,000-row asset. REQ3: there is no batch cursor, no persisted progress, no resume, and no indexing-state signal for search to display; a kill mid-import leaves the transaction rolled back and the whole import restarts, and the guard is 'does any non-user food row exist', so a partially committed import would be treated as complete and the catalogue would be permanently truncated. AC2 ('killed at 40 percent ... resumes and final row count exactly matches') cannot happen. REQ2/AC1 (shell interactive within 2.0 s while import continues) is not tested and is moot in the current design because import is triggered lazily by a nutrition query rather than at startup. There is no version record for the food catalogue, so unlike exercises it cannot be updated by shipping a new version. REQ5/AC4 unmet - no 100,000-food fixture exists. The 30-vs-100,000 figure is arguably a BACKLOG DEFECT of the same family as the exercise count, but the batching, resumability and status requirements are independent of scale and none of them is implemented.

evidence: REQ1 is met for exercises: src/Forge.Domain/Training/Exercise.cs:52 carries IsUserCreated as the source marker, src/Forge.App/Features/Exercises/ExerciseDataStore.cs:78-81 sets it in the store rather than trusting the caller ('so it must not depend on every call site remembering to set it'), and ExerciseDataStore.cs:136-139 refuses to delete a shipped catalogue movement. REQ2 is met in the direction that matters most: SeedContentImporter.cs:55-59 skips any existing row flagged IsUserCreated when a new catalogue version is applied, so a user's own movements survive a refresh - covered by SeedContentImporterTests. REQ3 is met for exercises by soft delete: shipped rows are never physically removed, so a historical SetEntry.ExerciseId still resolves.
gaps: AC1 is unmet as written. There is no override entity - a user cannot rename a catalogue exercise while leaving the base row to update separately. src/Forge.App/Features/Exercises/ExerciseDataStore.cs:94-116 UpdateAsync writes straight onto the catalogue row, and SeedContentImporter.cs:61-67 then overwrites Name, Pattern, PrimaryMuscle, Equipment and all guidance fields on the next catalogue version because the row is not IsUserCreated. So an edit to a shipped exercise is silently reverted by the next catalogue bump - the exact behaviour the criterion forbids. AC2 is unmet for foods: src/Forge.Domain/Nutrition/FoodItem.cs FoodLogEntry stores FoodItemId plus a ServingSnapshot (serving name, quantity, grams) but no snapshot of the food's display name, so a historical meal depends on a live join to FoodItem; if that row is soft-deleted the central query filter hides it and the entry has no name to render. Foods also have no catalogue-version import path at all (see S04.03.02), so 'a new catalogue version' cannot happen for them. The named files src/Forge.Domain/Catalogues and src/Forge.Infrastructure/Catalogues/CatalogueUpdateService.cs do not exist. REQ5/AC4 unmet; AC3 ungroundable by reading.

evidence: The abstraction is clean and genuinely used: src/Forge.Core/Abstractions/Data/IRepository.cs and IDataSession.cs expose no EF type, and 13 app services take IDataSessionFactory. 47 HasIndex declarations across the configurations cover the important composite shapes, notably (UserProfileId, StartedUtc), (UserProfileId, CompletedUtc) and (UserProfileId, ExerciseId, CompletedUtc) in Training/TrainingConfigurations.cs:84-117. A 250 ms search debounce exists in Features/Nutrition/ViewModels/NutritionViewModels.cs:227-231, and barcode lookup is backed by a unique filtered index on Gtin14 (Nutrition/BarcodeConfigurations.cs:36).
gaps: The feature outcome - 'fast, cancellable operations' - is not achievable through the abstraction as designed. IRepository<T> has no query surface: GetAsync by id, ListAsync for the whole table, and nothing else. Every filter, sort and top-N in the app therefore runs in memory over a fully materialised table. Combined with the documented 469 ms per connection open, none of the sub-150 ms and sub-200 ms budgets in this feature can be met at the stated scale, and none of them is measured: no 50,000-set or 100,000-food fixture exists, and tests/Forge.Infrastructure.Tests/Persistence/QueryPlanTests.cs does not exist.

evidence: AC1 is met exactly. src/Forge.Core/Abstractions/Data/IRepository.cs declares GetAsync, ListAsync, AddAsync, UpdateAsync and SoftDeleteAsync using only Guid, CancellationToken, IReadOnlyList<T> and the domain entity - no IQueryable, no DbSet, no EF type - and IDataSession.cs/IUnitOfWork.cs are equally clean; tests/Forge.Core.Tests/Architecture/DependencyRuleTests.cs asserts the whole Forge.Core assembly references no UI or persistence framework. REQ1 is satisfied generically rather than per-aggregate: IRepository<T> is constrained to Entity and IDataSession.Repository<T>() serves every listed aggregate. REQ3 is met and is the strongest part of this story: IDataSession extends IUnitOfWork and hands out repositories that all share one context (EfDataSession.cs:17-32), which structurally prevents the separately-resolved-repository trap; every method takes a CancellationToken; and tests/Forge.Infrastructure.Tests/Persistence/DataSessionTests.cs:38 (Writes_through_different_repositories_commit_in_one_save) and :61 (Pending_writes_are_discarded_when_the_session_is_disposed_without_saving) pin both halves of the unit-of-work contract, which is most of AC2. tools/ci/Test-DataAccessPatterns.ps1 enforces the pattern in CI.
gaps: The abstraction has no query surface, and that is a substantive design gap rather than a stylistic one. src/Forge.Infrastructure/Persistence/Repositories/EfRepository.cs:17-18 implements ListAsync as dbContext.Set<T>().ToListAsync() - the entire table - so every consumer filters, sorts and pages in memory. NutritionPersistenceService.SearchFoodsAsync (lines 103-123) is the clearest consequence: it calls foods.ListAsync then does an in-memory Contains over every row on each debounced keystroke. At the scales this epic specifies that is unworkable, and it means REQ2's 'never return IQueryable' was satisfied by removing querying rather than by abstracting it. AC2's negative half - one save fails, both writes roll back - is not directly tested; DataSessionTests covers commit-together and discard-on-dispose but not a failed SaveChanges. REQ5/AC4 unmet: no 50,000-set or 100,000-food fixture exists. AC3 ungroundable by reading. The named path src/Forge.Core/Abstractions/Persistence is actually src/Forge.Core/Abstractions/Data.

evidence: The index design is right and is the substance of this story. src/Forge.Infrastructure/Persistence/Configurations/Training/TrainingConfigurations.cs declares exactly the composite indexes these queries need: line 84 (UserProfileId, StartedUtc) and line 89 (UserProfileId, CompletedUtc) for the latest-workouts query, and lines 116-117 (ExerciseId, CompletedUtc) and (UserProfileId, ExerciseId, CompletedUtc) for the latest-sets-for-one-exercise query. Workout/WorkoutConfigurations.cs:25-27 adds a unique index on WorkoutSessionId. src/Forge.Domain/Common/Entity.cs:29 uses Guid.CreateVersion7 specifically so keys stay time-ordered and index locality survives the ~50,000-row growth this story describes - the reasoning is written out in the type's remarks.
gaps: Nothing is measured and nothing can currently reach these indexes. REQ1 unmet: no 5-sessions-a-week-for-3-years fixture exists anywhere under tests/ (a grep for 50000/50_000 over tests/ finds only an unrelated byte count). AC1 and AC2 unmet: tests/Forge.Infrastructure.Tests/Persistence/QueryPlanTests.cs does not exist, no p95 duration is recorded anywhere, and no EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN assertion exists in the repository. More seriously, the repository abstraction cannot express either query: IRepository<T> offers only ListAsync over the whole table (EfRepository.cs:17-18), so 'latest 100 workouts' and 'latest 500 sets for one exercise' are performed by materialising every row and sorting in memory - the indexes are declared but the app's own data path does not use them. Two ungrounded criteria: the 150 ms bounds and AC3's process-kill case both need execution rather than reading.

evidence: Some of the required machinery exists. src/Forge.App/Features/Nutrition/ViewModels/NutritionViewModels.cs:224-231 implements the 250 ms debounce with a CancellationTokenSource per keystroke, matching REQ2's debounce. Barcode lookup is properly indexed: src/Forge.Infrastructure/Persistence/Configurations/Nutrition/BarcodeConfigurations.cs:36 declares a unique index on Gtin14 filtered on DeletedUtc IS NULL, and src/Forge.App/Features/Scanning/Services/BarcodeCatalogueService.cs resolves an exact GTIN, which is the right shape for REQ3. FoodItemConfiguration.cs:18-19 indexes Name and Brand.
gaps: Search does not use any of it. src/Forge.App/Features/Nutrition/Services/NutritionPersistenceService.cs:103-123 calls foods.ListAsync(cancellationToken) - which EfRepository implements as ToListAsync over the entire FoodItem table - and then filters with an in-memory string Contains on Name and Brand. The Name/Brand indexes are therefore never used by the search path, and the query cost is linear in catalogue size with a full table materialisation per keystroke. There is no ranking of any kind (results are ordered alphabetically, not by relevance), and Take(20) returns 20 results where AC1 specifies 50. The named artefact src/Forge.Infrastructure/Persistence/Search/FoodSearchIndex.cs does not exist, and there is no FTS5 table, no trigram index and no prefix index anywhere in the migrations. REQ1's 100,000-item scale is not present - the shipped catalogue is 30 foods (src/Forge.Infrastructure/Content/food-catalogue.json), which is a BACKLOG DEFECT of the same family as the exercise count, but the architecture would not survive the stated scale regardless. The 200 ms, 100 ms and 10 MB allocation bounds are unmeasured and ungroundable by reading; no scale fixture exists to measure them against. AC3 ungroundable.

evidence: One real piece exists: src/Forge.Infrastructure/Persistence/DatabaseInitializer.cs:136-167 runs PRAGMA integrity_check on every startup, parses the result rows and returns a typed DatabaseInitializationStatus.Corrupt with the technical messages attached rather than attempting any automatic repair - which does satisfy the feature's 'without destructive automatic repair' principle.
gaps: Everything else is absent. There is no idle-time cadence, no quick_check, no abnormal-shutdown marker, no safety-copy service, no free-space precondition and no operation journal: a grep over src/ for 'quick_check|OperationJournal|SafetyCopy|abnormal|IntegrityService' returns exactly one match, the startup integrity_check above. None of the named directories (Persistence/Integrity, Persistence/Recovery) exists. And because F01.03 was never built there is no recovery surface for a Corrupt result to open, so a detected corruption is reported to a logger with no provider and then surfaces as an improvised per-screen error string.

evidence: src/Forge.Infrastructure/Persistence/DatabaseInitializer.cs:56-85 runs an integrity check as part of every startup and records the outcome as a typed result: RunIntegrityCheckAsync (lines 136-167) executes PRAGMA integrity_check over the live connection, collects every returned row, and treats a single 'ok' as success. A failure produces DatabaseInitializationStatus.Corrupt carrying the raw SQLite messages (lines 69-72), and the logged event contains only those technical strings - no user data - which satisfies REQ3's 'technical status only'. tests/Forge.Infrastructure.Tests/Persistence/DatabaseInitializerTests.cs covers the path.
gaps: The cadence, which is what the story is actually about, does not exist. REQ1 unmet: there is no weekly schedule and no idle detection - grep over src/ for quick_check returns nothing, and the check that does run is the expensive full integrity_check, on the cold-start critical path, on every single launch. REQ2 unmet: there is no abnormal-shutdown marker anywhere, so nothing distinguishes a clean exit from a crash and nothing escalates from quick to full. REQ3's second half unmet: nothing yields after 5 seconds if the device is no longer idle, because nothing is scheduled against idle in the first place. AC1 unmet: no last-check timestamp is stored anywhere, so 'the last check was over 7 days ago' cannot be evaluated. AC2 unmet for the same reason. The named file src/Forge.Infrastructure/Persistence/Integrity/DatabaseIntegrityService.cs does not exist. REQ5/AC4 unmet - no scale fixture; AC3 ungroundable by reading.

evidence: The named file src/Forge.Infrastructure/Persistence/Recovery/DatabaseSafetyCopyService.cs does not exist, nor does the Persistence/Recovery directory. A grep over src/ for 'SafetyCopy' returns zero matches, and for free-space checks (DriveInfo, AvailableFreeSpace) likewise nothing. There is no repair action to guard: no recovery surface exists at all (see S01.03.02 and F04.05). The nearest related code is src/Forge.Infrastructure/Backup/ForgeBackupService.cs, which is the user-initiated encrypted backup feature owned by E26 - it is not invoked before any recovery action, has no retention cap of two automatic copies, and is not triggered by corruption detection. One partial precedent does exist for the underlying technique: LocalDatabaseEncryption.ConvertAsync (LocalDatabaseEncryption.cs:158-182) writes to a .encrypting side file and only replaces the original on success, so the encryption upgrade path is interruption-safe - but that is a single specific conversion, not the general pre-repair safety copy this story specifies.
gaps: All three requirements are unmet: no encrypted safety copy is created before any destructive action, no two-copy retention policy exists, and no free-space precondition is evaluated. AC1 and AC2 therefore both fail - there is no repair action, no copy and no 'exact additional space required' message anywhere in the codebase. REQ5/AC4 unmet; AC3 ungroundable by reading.

evidence: The named file src/Forge.Infrastructure/Persistence/Recovery/OperationJournal.cs does not exist and neither does the directory. A grep over src/ for OperationJournal returns zero matches, and there is no operation-marker entity in src/Forge.Infrastructure/Persistence/Configurations - the mapped set is Profile, Training, Planning, Workout, Nutrition, Recovery (readiness/soreness) and Engagement, with no journal or marker table. Startup does not scan for incomplete operations: src/Forge.App/Composition/ForgeStartup.cs:106-141 resolves the key, upgrades encryption, migrates, integrity-checks and imports seed content, and then finishes.
gaps: All three requirements are unmet. No critical write records an operation id before commit or marks it complete after (REQ1); nothing scans incomplete operations at startup (REQ2); there is no reconciliation routine at all, so idempotency and the 500 ms/100 marker budget are moot (REQ3). AC1 and AC2 both fail. Note that the underlying risk is partly mitigated by other means rather than by this story: set logging commits through a single EF SaveChanges inside one transaction (src/Forge.App/Features/Workout/WorkoutPersistenceService.cs:176-186), so a kill mid-write rolls back rather than leaving an orphan - but that is a property of the write path, not the journal-and-reconcile mechanism specified here, and nothing verifies it. REQ5/AC4 unmet; AC3 ungroundable by reading.
